summary: Write the feature guide: one page per product area on the cheap model, and one map of the whole codebase

guide.what_it_is_for: This area is the set of places a signed-in person can go inside the app: the new-chat home, past chats, search, archived and pinned chats, projects, AGI Work tasks, schedules, coding sessions, devices, the Library, shared items, agents, skills, plugins, connected accounts, models, usage, billing, settings, admin, developer keys and help. It is how a person finds and returns to everything the account holds. The web app owns most of these screens, and the other apps reuse them or build their own version on the same server routes.
guide.who_uses_it: Mostly every signed-in user. Some destinations depend on the plan: schedules need a plan that allows scheduled tasks (SchedulesPage.tsx:306), projects have a per-plan count limit (free-plan-entitlements.ts:10), and file storage has a per-plan byte limit (free-plan-entitlements.ts:18). Workspace members only see Shared items, Members and Sharing (org membership is required, organization/shared/route.ts:57). Only people with the sharing right can change what is shared (org-sharing-service.ts:82). Workspace admin pages are for admins. Developer keys are for people who use the API.

features.name: New chat and past chats
features.use: Open an empty chat with a ready composer, or open an old chat to read it and carry on.
how_people_use_it: Web: go to /chat for a new chat, or click a chat in the sidebar to go to /chat/<id>.
Mobile: tap New chat or pick a chat from the drawer.
CLI: start the TUI for a new chat, or resume a session with --session <id>.
/agi-work opens the same /chat page with AGI Work mode already on.
how_it_should_work: Both web routes render the same chat root, so a link and the sidebar land in the same place.
A past chat shows its transcript and the composer works at once.
The page title comes from the chat title on the server (conversationMetadata).
If the chat does not exist or is deleted, the person should see a not-found or error state (not-found.tsx and error.tsx exist under app/chat). I did not open them.
features.on_each_app: Web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome all show done in the brief. Desktop shows the hosted web app, as AGENTS.md says.

features.name: Search, archived and pinned chats
features.use: Find a chat by words, keep old chats out of the way and restore them, and keep important chats at the top.
how_people_use_it: Web: press Cmd/Ctrl+K or click the search button in the sidebar header and type. Opening /chat?search=true also opens it.
Web: open Settings > Archived chats (/settings/archived) to see archived chats, restore them or delete them. The sidebar also has an archived view.
Pinned chats are listed first in the sidebar.
Mobile: search from the drawer or Chats list; archived chats are under Settings > Archived chats.
CLI: agi --search <text>; session Archive/Unarchive and a list of archived sessions.
how_it_should_work: Search sends the words to /api/search, which matches chat titles and message text with a case-insensitive contains match. It also returns projects, files and schedules.
Archived chats are left out of search unless includeArchived is set.
The archived list shows a loading state, an error with Retry, and the empty text 'No archived chats'.
Delete from the archived list moves chats to Recently deleted, where they can be restored for 30 days. A confirmation names this.
Archiving a chat also clears its pin (bulk route sets pinned = false).
features.on_each_app: Pinned: web, desktop and mobile only. CLI and VS Code show missing in the brief. Archived: not in the Chrome extension. Search and archived on mobile use the same /api/chat/conversations route with archived=only.

features.name: Projects: list, overview, chats, instructions
features.use: Group chats, files and instructions for one piece of work, and open it from one list.
how_people_use_it: Web: click Projects in the sidebar (/chat/projects), create one, open it.
A project page has tabs Chats, Artifacts, Work, Sources and Scheduled, plus a composer that starts a new chat in the project.
Open the project settings dialog to edit name, description, instructions, default model and personalisation switches.
Mobile: Projects tab or drawer item; CLI: agi projects (list, create, add-file, archive, delete).
how_it_should_work: The list loads 50 at a time and lets the person load more.
Creating a project over the plan's project limit is refused with a message that names the plan and the limit.
Instructions apply only to chats in that project. A switch decides whether the account profile and instructions also apply.
A banner appears when a project holds 80 or more chats.
If a project cannot be found, the page shows a not-found or error state with retry.
features.on_each_app: Web, desktop, mobile and CLI done. VS Code has project actions. Chrome is unverified. S4.08 CLI is missing.

features.name: Project sources, members, memory and notebook
features.use: Give a project its own files, decide who can see it, and keep what it has remembered apart from account memory.
how_people_use_it: Web: open the Sources tab to add or remove files; a Sources side panel opens over the project.
Use the project menu > Share to add people and pick Can view, Can edit or No access.
Open the project settings dialog to see the project memory panel and switch off use of global memory.
CLI: agi projects add-file; agi memory add --project-scoped keeps a memory with a linked project.
how_it_should_work: Listing sources returns each file with its index state and the account's storage use.
Adding a file is checked against the plan's storage limit; over the limit the message says to delete a file or upgrade.
Only the project owner or a person with sharing rights can change access. Viewers cannot be given edit access.
Project memory is separate from account memory and shows 'Cloud memory is unavailable' until the account is ready.
features.on_each_app: Sources: web, desktop and mobile; CLI and Chrome missing. Members: web and desktop only. Memory: web, desktop and CLI. Notebook workspace: web and desktop only.

features.name: AGI Work tasks, approvals and details
features.use: Give the assistant a goal it carries out in many steps, then watch the runs, read what happened and answer anything it needs from you.
how_people_use_it: Web: switch the composer to AGI Work mode on /chat (or go to /agi-work), or click Start work on /tasks.
On /tasks use the filters Active, Needs you, All, Archived and the List or Board layout. Click a run to open its detail.
In a run that waits, click Approve or Reject (optionally with guidance).
Mobile: AGI Work in the drawer opens the runs list and a detail sheet.
how_it_should_work: Runs come from the cloud runs route. 'Needs you' shows runs waiting for input, approval or paused.
If another device already answered an approval, the person sees 'Another device already answered this approval.' If it expired, the message says it can no longer continue.
Archive is only shown where the surface can reach the archive route.
The layout choice is remembered in the browser.
features.on_each_app: Web, desktop, mobile done. VS Code has task trees and approvals. CLI missing. Chrome side panel has the work home; the rest is unverified. Mobile gates AGI Work on the cloudTasks flag.

features.name: Scheduled tasks and routine details
features.use: Run a prompt again on a repeating schedule and look at each run's results.
how_people_use_it: Web: open /chat/schedules, pick a template or create a schedule, then use the card menu to edit, pause, run now or delete.
Open a schedule card to see its prompt, next run and run history.
CLI: agi schedules (subcommands). Mobile: Schedules in the drawer.
how_it_should_work: If the plan allows zero scheduled tasks, the create action is not offered.
Run now uses a fresh idempotency key so a double click does not run twice.
A run that needs approval can be approved or rejected from its history.
Rows show a busy state per row and an error message per row.
features.on_each_app: Web, desktop, mobile, CLI and Chrome done. VS Code has no manager row in the brief but has routine details.

features.name: Coding sessions
features.use: Start a coding task on a repository in an isolated cloud environment, then follow it and steer the next turn.
how_people_use_it: Web: open /code, describe the task, choose a repository or runtime. A session opens at /code/<id>.
In the session, read the transcript, view changes, and type the next instruction.
Mobile: Code in the drawer; CLI: agi code (start, list, show, open, approvals, approve, reject).
how_it_should_work: A new session starts a turn that appears in the transcript while it runs.
Approvals the session waits on can be approved or rejected.
Not seen in the code I read: the exact plan gate for Code.
features.on_each_app: Web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code done. Chrome missing.

features.name: Devices and remote sessions
features.use: See which of your own devices are linked and remove or rename them, and follow a session running on another device.
how_people_use_it: Web: Settings > Account > Linked devices: read each device's state, rename it, or unlink it.
CLI: agi devices lists devices (JSON option).
Mobile: Companion screens show account computers and a remote code session view.
how_it_should_work: The list shows device type, platform, online state, signed in or out and last seen.
Unlink asks first and names what stops working.
A failed load shows 'Unable to load linked devices.'
features.on_each_app: Devices: web, desktop done; mobile screens exist but companion and dispatch are false in the v1 flags (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts), so I expect them hidden in this build; CLI has a devices command although the brief says missing. Remote viewer exists only on mobile.

features.name: Library, artifacts, images and media jobs
features.use: One place for everything the account made or uploaded, with filters, plus a way to edit an artifact and see image and video jobs.
how_people_use_it: Web: open /chat/library and use the tabs All, Images, Videos, Documents, Artifacts, Uploads, Generated files.
/chat/artifacts redirects to the Library with the artifact filter; /chat/images redirects to the Images tab.
Open an item to preview it, or download it.
Open an artifact and edit it directly; an edit becomes a new version.
The media jobs section lists image and video jobs with status.
how_it_should_work: The Library lists 24 or so items a page from /api/library with kind, sort, surface, origin and search filters.
Each job shows status (queued, running, failed, done) and an error only when failed.
Temporary chats' jobs are hidden.
Deleted items carry an erase-after date (30-day recovery window).
features.on_each_app: Library: web, desktop, mobile, CLI. Artifact gallery: all but Chrome unverified. Editor: web and desktop only. Image studio: web and desktop 'unverified'; web has no separate studio route, only a redirect to the Library. Mobile has an image area editor. Media jobs: web, desktop, mobile.

features.name: Shared items
features.use: See what the workspace has shared: projects, chats, artifacts and connectors, with the access level of each.
how_people_use_it: Web: open /workspace/sharing.
Open a shared project from its row.
how_it_should_work: The page needs workspace membership.
An empty list says nothing is shared yet and tells the person how to share a chat.
Only the sharer or a sharing manager can withdraw a share.

features.name: Agents (custom assistants)
features.use: Create and manage your own assistants with their own instructions, files, tools and starter prompts.
how_people_use_it: Web: open /chat/agents, click New, fill in instructions, conversation starters, model and tools, then save.
Mobile: Agents in the drawer (folded menu).

Starters are capped (AGENT_STARTERS_MAX).

features.name: Skills, plugins and connected accounts
features.use: Add abilities to the assistant: skills, plugins and links to other services.
how_people_use_it: Web: /chat/customize?section=skills, plugins or connectors redirects to the matching settings pane. /settings/connections opens Connectors.
Connect, reconnect or disconnect each service from its row.
CLI: agi plugin; TUI skill and plugin screens.
how_it_should_work: Signed-out visitors to /settings/connections see a sign-in prompt instead.
After a GitHub connect, a toast shows success or error.
Plugin install, update and remove go through the plugins routes.
features.on_each_app: Skills: web, desktop, CLI, VS Code; mobile has a skills screen not listed in the brief. Plugins: not on mobile. Connected accounts: not in CLI (CLI has a connectors command although the brief says missing).

features.name: Models, usage, billing and settings
features.use: Pick a model, see how much of the plan is used, see plan and invoices, and change personal preferences.
how_people_use_it: Web: open the model picker in the composer footer to see the catalogue; set a default in Settings > General.
Settings > Usage shows limits, resets and history. Settings > Billing shows plan, invoices, overage switch.
Open /settings/general, /settings/usage, /settings/billing: each redirects to the chat page with the settings panel open on that section.
how_it_should_work: The catalogue is built on the server from the model registry, route health and the person's plan. A model with no working route is hidden or marked.
Free users should see only an Upgrade prompt on usage, not meters (owner decision).
The overage switch is saved immediately and rolled back if saving fails.
Top-up result is announced with a message after checkout.
features.on_each_app: Usage is done on every app. Billing is partial on web, desktop and mobile. Mobile billing is turned off in v1 by FEATURES.billing = false.

features.name: Workspace admin, developer console and help
features.use: Manage members and policies, create API keys and see their use, and reach help and send feedback.
how_people_use_it: Web: /workspace/people lists members, roles, seats and invitations; the workspace nav has more pages (sharing, usage, policy, roles and others).
/developers shows keys; create or revoke a key and see use per key.
Account menu > Help; the composer feedback dialog sends a message with an optional screenshot.
how_it_should_work: Feedback needs text and is blocked while sending or while a screenshot is captured.
API usage is counted per key for the current month.
Admin pages require workspace admin rights.
features.on_each_app: Admin: web and desktop. Developer console: web and desktop only (the CLI also has a keys command). Help: all apps, Chrome unverified.

how_it_works.detail: A person goes to a web address like /chat, /chat/<id>, /tasks, /chat/library. Some are plain pages; others redirect to a pane in the settings panel or to the Library.
Pages are wrapped in the app shell with the sidebar. The sidebar items (Chat, Projects, Library, and so on) come from one list. The chat root loads the chat page without server rendering.
Settings routes turn the pane name into a link that opens the modal. Only listed pane names are allowed so a bad link cannot show an empty modal.
The screen calls a route under /api (projects, schedules, library, search, custom-agents, settings/devices and others). Routes check the rate limit and the CSRF token on writes.

how_it_works.step: Scope the data to the person
how_it_works.detail: Routes get a database handle limited to the signed-in user and workspace, so a query only sees that person's rows. Shared projects are read through a readable-project check.
Plan tiers set how many projects, how many scheduled tasks and how many bytes of files a person may hold. The server refuses with a message naming the plan.
The search dialog calls the search service, which sends one request to /api/search. The server runs case-insensitive matches on chat titles, project names, files, schedules and message text.

Tasks and Library are drawn by shared components in the unified chat package. Web hands them a transport object (how to fetch, open, archive); the shared screen does the rest. Mobile has its own native screens on the same routes.
The CLI calls the same hosted routes through a client (schedules, library, projects, artifacts, memory, devices, code). Mobile hides parts by a flag file.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the sidebar (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx), the tasks screen and the library screen (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks and library), the plan limits in the types package, and the cloud contracts used by routes and clients. Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it gets the web screens. Separate per app: mobile has its own native screens under apps/mobile/src/features and its drawer; the CLI has Rust commands under apps/cli/src; VS Code has tree views and commands under apps/extension-vscode/src; Chrome has its own side panel in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area decides how the chat screen is laid out: where the conversation sits, how wide it is, which side panels open beside it, and how it changes on a phone, a tablet or a wide window. It also covers panels that can be resized, hidden, pulled into their own window, or printed. A good layout keeps the reply readable, keeps the composer (the text box) in reach, and remembers what the person set up.
guide.who_uses_it: Every user of every app. The layout code has no plan gate. The web and desktop code-session panes (tiled or stacked) only appear in the Code page, and only when the page turns them on (the `enabled` input of the pane hook, apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-code-panes.ts:25-34). The desktop floating Quick Ask window and detachable panels only exist in the Electron desktop app.

features.name: Start view and reading column
features.use: An empty chat shows a greeting with a centred composer. Messages sit in a centred, narrow column. Tables can go wider and keep their header row visible.
how_people_use_it: Open a new chat and see the greeting and the composer in the middle.
Send a message; the conversation fills a centred column.
Widen the window; the text column stays the same width and stays centred.
Scroll a long table; the header row stays pinned.
how_it_should_work: Web: with no messages, the page shows a greeting banner and a centred composer (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6651, 7637). Once there are messages, the transcript replaces it.
Notices and message rows use `max-w-3xl` with `mx-auto` (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:1939, 2015).
Mobile caps the reading column at 720 points and centres it (apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts:3-8).
Table header cells use `sticky top-0` (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx:584).
A table can be opened wider than the column; the brief points at MarkdownTable.tsx. I did not open the expanded view in detail.
features.on_each_app: Start view: all six apps are marked done. Reading width: web, desktop, mobile, VS Code and Chrome done, CLI not listed. Data layout: web and desktop done, Chrome unverified. Sticky headers: web and desktop done; mobile, VS Code and Chrome missing. Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it gets the web code.

features.name: Side panels beside the chat (artifact, sources, work)
features.use: An artifact, a research source list or a work-session panel opens on the right of the conversation. The person can drag it wider or narrower.
how_people_use_it: Open an artifact or research panel from a message.
Drag the thin bar on the panel's left edge to resize it.
Focus the bar and press Left or Right arrow to change width by 24 pixels, Home for the minimum, End for the maximum.
how_it_should_work: The bar is a `separator` with a label such as 'Resize artifacts panel' (apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx:35-45; ArtifactsPanel.tsx:690; ResearchPanel.tsx:398; WorkSessionPanel.tsx:1079).
Width is clamped to 280 to 900 pixels (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts:6-11) and the panel has a 280 pixel minimum (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:686).
The conversation takes the remaining space beside it.
Opening the artifact panel also collapses the left sidebar (uiStore.ts:57).
features.on_each_app: Artifact split view: web, desktop and VS Code done. Source inspector: web and desktop done; CLI and VS Code missing. Resize: web and desktop only. VS Code artifacts are opened by a command (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactActions.ts); I did not read how it is placed. Chrome width limits are unverified.

features.name: Code workspace and several sessions at once
features.use: A coding session shows the chat next to its code work. Up to three sessions can sit side by side or one above another.
how_people_use_it: On the Code page, open a session from the rail and choose to split it into a new pane.
Switch between tiled and stacked with the layout toggle.
Press Cmd or Ctrl plus backslash to close the focused pane.
VS Code: use the chat view or editor panel and move it to another edge with the editor's own docking.
how_it_should_work: A hook keeps the list of panes, the focused pane and the layout, which starts as `tiled` (use-code-panes.ts:41).
The most panes is 3 including the main one (use-code-panes.ts:33, 86).
Selecting a session already open focuses it; if the limit is reached it replaces the focused pane (use-code-panes.ts:74-98).
The page marks its container with `data-pane-layout` and styles tiled and stacked in CloudCodePage.module.css:2631-2644.
When the main pane closes, the next pane is promoted (use-code-panes.ts:62-68).
features.on_each_app: Web and desktop done (desktop shows the web page). CLI has a TUI with chat and tool output marked done. VS Code uses its own sidebar and editor panel (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/chatSetup.ts:60). Mobile and Chrome: not listed. Dockable panels: only VS Code (web and desktop missing).

features.name: Collapsible navigation and responsive shell
features.use: The conversation list can be hidden. On smaller screens panels cover the chat or become sheets, and tablets get a two-column view. The left sidebar cannot be dragged to a new width.
how_people_use_it: Click the sidebar toggle to collapse or reopen the conversation list.
On a phone, swipe from the left edge or tap the menu to open the drawer.
Narrow the web window; panels cover the chat with a dimmed backdrop.
Open the keyboard on a phone; the composer moves up with it.
how_it_should_work: Web shell layout has three tiers: under 768 wide is compact with a drawer, 1024 and over is regular with a permanent sidebar, and between is tablet (app-shell-layout.ts:5-6, 27-46). Tablet portrait shows an icon rail; tablet landscape keeps the sidebar.
The web artifact panel becomes a full-screen overlay under 640 wide (ARTIFACT_PANEL_OVERLAY_QUERY, apps/web/features/chat/stores/artifacts-store.ts:38; ArtifactsPanel.tsx:669-690).

Mobile uses a permanent drawer once the window is at least 1000 wide (280 drawer plus 720 content); otherwise an overlay drawer up to 300 wide (useResponsiveLayout.ts:3-10, 23-30). Content grids use 1, 2 or 3 columns.
Mobile pickers use sheets (ModelPickerSheet.tsx, AddToChatSheet.tsx are named by the brief).
Safe areas and keyboard: mobile chat screen handles the keyboard (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1277-1286); web uses CSS in globals.css:1416 (I did not open it).
Left sidebar resize: not present anywhere (brief marks web, desktop, mobile missing).
features.on_each_app: Collapse: web, desktop, mobile, VS Code, Chrome done. Stacking panels: web, desktop, mobile done; Chrome unverified. Bottom sheets: web and mobile done. Tablet two columns: web and mobile done. Safe area and keyboard: web and mobile. Sidebar resize: missing on web, desktop and mobile.

features.name: Composer at the bottom, growing and full-screen editing
features.use: The text box stays at the bottom while messages scroll above it. It grows with long text, and can open in a larger editor.
how_people_use_it: Type a long message; the box grows.
Scroll the conversation; the composer, header and side panels do not move.
Open the expanded editor on web or mobile for long text; in the CLI use the external editor key.
how_it_should_work: Transcript scrolls in its own region (ChatMessageList.tsx; MessageList.tsx on mobile) and the composer sits outside it (WebChatPage.tsx; ChatComposerNew.tsx).
The box has a growth limit then scrolls inside.
Closing the full editor returns to the chat with the text kept.

features.name: Detachable panels and floating Quick Ask

guide.what_it_is_for: This area is the set of larger screen parts that are built from smaller controls: pickers (model, file, project, workspace, repository, branch, device), lists and grids (library, tables, timelines, task board), review panels (diffs, versions, sources) and status cards (usage, credits, approvals, progress, notifications). A person uses them to choose what a chat or task works with, to watch it run, and to check and approve the result. They matter because every app needs the same choices and the same safety prompts, and a wrong or silent state here (a locked model that looks open, a missing warning) misleads the person.
guide.who_uses_it: Mostly every signed-in user. Some parts depend on plan: the model picker marks models that need a higher plan and sends the person to upgrade; Free users see an "Upgrade" prompt in usage instead of the plan meters; the Code repository and branch pickers need the cloud sandbox switched on for the server; workspace switching only matters to people who belong to a team workspace; the member and recipient picker is for people who share or invite inside a workspace or project. Developers use the repository, branch, diff and command palette parts.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area is everything attached to a message the person sent: who sent it, the text, attached files, the context chips, when it was sent, and the actions on it (copy, edit, resend, branch, page between versions). It also covers what happens when a send is queued, fails or is retried, and how an unsent draft is kept. It lets people fix a prompt, redo a turn or fork a conversation without retyping, and it keeps the transcript honest about what was actually sent.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user of the chat surfaces. The web code shows no plan gate on the message actions themselves. Branching is a server call that counts against the daily allowance of a free account (assertFreeDailyAllowance in apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:204), so Free users can be refused when the daily limit is used up. Draft sync to the server is skipped for temporary conversations and for conversations that hold Local-model turns.

how_it_works.detail: The chat page maps stored messages to MessageBubble. A user row gets role data, a hidden 'You said:' heading and a right-aligned bubble.
The bubble draws the text, then attachments and MessageContextChips from message metadata.
A layout effect measures the text height against 320px and sets an overflow flag; a button toggles expansion.
Hover/focus reveals Retry, Edit, Copy and a '...' menu with the send time and Branch. The row is always visible on touch.
The bubble asks the page via the inline-edit context. The page plans the edit, then resubmits as a sibling (variants on) or replaces after a confirm (variants off).
VariantPager shows n/m and calls onSelectVariant with the previous or next message id; the page switches the active path.
If the last user message has no good reply, the banner offers Retry, which rolls back that turn and sends it again.
The hook posts to the branches route; the route validates, applies the rate limit and calls forkConversation, which copies the thread in a transaction.
The composer queues follow-ups in memory; the draft hook saves unsent text to the conversation row with a revision.

Chips for the skill and connector prompt and resources sent with a message.

Owns edit, regenerate/retry, branch and the failure banner; passes handlers to bubbles.
Decides which user message the Retry banner resends.
Switch for keeping old versions versus replacing them.
Client call that creates a branch and opens it.
Server code that copies a thread up to a message into a new conversation.
Saves and reconciles the unsent draft with the server.
Composer with the queued-follow-up list.
Mobile bubble, copy, edit modal and pager.
VS Code transcript with delivery-state labels.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area covers every way a person finds things: searching old chats, projects, library files and artifacts, finding text inside one chat, and letting the assistant search the web or connected work apps. It also covers how answers show their sources (cards, citation hover previews, source lists) and what the person sees when a search finds nothing or fails. It matters because people trust an answer only if they can see where it came from, and because they need to get back to past work fast.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user can search their own chats, projects and library. Web search by the assistant is gated by the plan capability "canUseWebSearch" and by whether the chosen model or the service has a search route; the Free plan has a monthly cap of 20 search calls (search-budget.ts:36). Company-source (connector) search needs a plan that includes connectors, a released-connectors switch and a kill switch that is open. The "scheduled" search category needs workspace access. Developers can use the API with domain allow and deny lists. The CLI web search uses the user's own search key.

features.name: Find inside the open chat
features.use: Jump between the messages in one open conversation that contain some text.
how_people_use_it: Web and Desktop: press Cmd+F or Ctrl+F inside a chat; a search bar appears above the messages.
Type the text; the match count shows; press Enter for the next match and Shift+Enter for the previous one, or click the up and down arrows.
Press Escape or the close button to leave search.
CLI (full-screen chat): type /find followed by the text.
how_it_should_work: Matching is case-insensitive on the text as shown on screen, and the list scrolls to the matching message and centres it, wrapping from last to first.
Matched text is highlighted in the page.
With no matches the next/previous arrows are disabled.
Closing the bar clears the query.

CLI lists matching lines as '#<message number> <who> <line>' (first 120 characters), shows at most a fixed number (FIND_RESULT_LIMIT) with '... N more', and says 'Nothing in this conversation matches ...' when empty. It does not jump; it only lists.
features.on_each_app: Web done. Desktop done (it shows the hosted web app, so it is the same code). Mobile missing. CLI done as a /find listing, not a jump. VS Code missing. Chrome missing.

features.name: Global search dialog and chat history search
features.use: One Search window that finds past chats (by title and by message text), projects, library files, artifacts, code sessions and scheduled tasks, with filters, recent searches and previews.
how_people_use_it: Web and Desktop: open Search from the sidebar or the 'open-search' shortcut.
Type at least 2 characters.
Pick a category chip: All, Artifacts, Sessions, Code, Projects, Scheduled (desktop app also gets 'Local Code').
For All or Sessions, open Filters: message type (all, mine, AI, system), From date, To date, 'Include archived conversations'; 'Clear Filters' resets.
Before typing, click a recent search or a 'frequent search' chip to run it; 'Clear' next to Recent Searches asks for confirmation and then wipes the history.
Click a result to open it.
Mobile: type in the chats list search; searching also covers projects, files, library images and artifacts shown in groups.
CLI: '/sessions search <query>' in the line chat, or 'agi --search <query>' (add --output-format json for all matches).
VS Code: open session history and type in the pick list (2+ characters) or use the sessions sheet search box.
Chrome extension: type in the history drawer search of the side panel.
how_it_should_work: Only the user's own, non-deleted, non-temporary chats are searched; archived ones are left out unless 'include archived' is on.
Search is blocked with a clear message if the workspace's data region cannot be confirmed.
Setting a role or date filter turns off the indexed document search and uses plain row matching only.
Results show title, a snippet with the matched text, and a type label (Title, Project, File, Artifact, Report, Code session, Project source, Scheduled).

Waiting shows a spinner 'Searching workspace'; empty shows 'No results found - Try different keywords or clear filters'; failure shows 'Search could not be completed' with a Retry button; a crash shows 'Search unavailable'.
Each real search is recorded in the user's search history unless the caller asks not to track it.
Mobile on a Cloud account tries the server first and falls back to on-device messages if the server call fails, marking the search as failed; Local mode only searches the phone.
CLI search lists at most 50 most recent sessions and prints a notice when there are more.
features.on_each_app: Web done (full dialog with filters, history, suggestions). Desktop done (same dialog plus Local Code category). Mobile done for chats and projects, but no date filter and no suggestions. CLI done for chat history only (no projects, no preview). VS Code done for chat history only. Chrome done for chat history (local drawer search). Date filters and suggestions exist on Web and Desktop only.

features.name: Search Projects, Library and artifacts
features.use: Find a project, a saved file or image, or an artifact by name or prompt.
how_people_use_it: Web and Desktop: open Library and type in 'Search files and projects'; pick a tab (All, Images, Videos, Documents, Artifacts, Uploads, Generated files) to narrow; /chat/artifacts redirects to the Library Artifacts view.
Mobile: use the search bar on the Projects tab ('Search projects') and the search inside Library.
Click or tap a result to open it.
how_it_should_work: Library search waits a short time after typing (debounce), then asks the server for items whose file name or prompt contains the text.
The server escapes special characters and returns pages with a 'has more' flag; deleted items only show in the recently deleted view.
Empty search shows everything for the chosen tab.
Folders in the All tab are filtered by name on the device.
Mobile library and artifact search runs on the device over what the phone already holds, including artifact content.
features.on_each_app: Web done. Desktop done (same shared Library). Mobile done (on-device). CLI missing. VS Code missing for Library (it has artifacts per the brief, not verified). Chrome missing.

features.name: Assistant searches the public web
features.use: A chat can look up current information on the internet and answer with sources; developers using the API can limit which sites it may use.
how_people_use_it: Just ask a question that needs fresh facts; search is automatic where available.

Web/Desktop/Mobile: the composer keeps web search on by itself when the chosen model or service has a search route; asking in words ('search the web for...') or time-bound phrases ('this year', 'who is the current president') makes search required for that turn.
CLI: '/search <question>' makes the next turn a web search; it needs a search key saved with 'agi login' or set in the environment.
VS Code: plus menu 'Set up web search' to save a search key for Local or own-key use.
API: send research_sources.allow_domains and deny_domains with the chat request.
how_it_should_work: Each search returns up to 5 results (title, link, snippet, date when known); at most 3 searches per normal answer and 10 for AGI Work turns; queries over 400 characters are cut.
One retry on a rate limit or server error, 15 second timeout.
Allowed and denied sites (up to 32 each) are passed to the search provider when 20 or fewer, and every result is checked again before the model sees it; a denied site wins over an allowed one.
Results show publication date and retrieval date when known.
If search is unavailable the answer must say so rather than invent sources.
Free plan is limited to 20 search calls per 30 days and the composer blocks sending a search request when the allowance is used up.
Local privacy mode refuses network access.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome, VS Code and CLI all have web search (CLI and VS Code Local/own-key need the user's own search key; the CLI supports two search services). Site restriction and include/exclude domains exist only in the API; no app screen exposes them. Freshness dates shown on Web, Desktop, Mobile; not CLI, VS Code or Chrome per the brief.

features.name: Search connected company sources
features.use: Let the assistant search the user's connected work apps (such as file storage, mail, chat) during a chat.
how_people_use_it: Connect an app in settings (connectors).
Ask a question that needs that data; the assistant calls the app's search tool.
Approve the action when asked (the CLI asks 'Allow connector action ...?').
Mobile: manage connectors in settings, Cloud connectors.
how_it_should_work: Connector tools are offered only if connectors are released, the plan includes them, the kill switch is open, and the model can use tools.
A chat can turn individual connectors off for that turn only.
Denied tools are never shown to the model.
Tools the plan limit cuts are reported to the client.
The user's saved allow/ask/deny choice decides whether approval is asked.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome are all marked done; the connection is made by the shared Cloud chat service, so it works the same in each. CLI shows approval prompts for connector actions.

features.name: Project knowledge collections
features.use: Put files into a project so every chat in that project searches them.
how_people_use_it: Open a project, go to its Sources tab, add files; wait for 'indexing' to finish.
Chat inside the project; the assistant draws on those files.
CLI: add a file to a project's knowledge; managed turns in a linked folder can search it.
Mobile: Project sources tab.
how_it_should_work: Files that fit are sent whole; larger files are searched and only matching passages are sent.
If the index has nothing yet, passages are chosen per request.
An archived, deleted or unavailable project blocks the chat with an error asking to remove the chat from the project or restore the project.
Failed indexing shows an error on the file.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and VS Code done; Chrome not applicable.

features.name: Follow-up questions and clarification choices
features.use: After an answer, offer tappable next questions; when a request is unclear, offer choices before answering.
how_people_use_it: Tap a suggested follow-up under the answer to send it.
When the assistant shows a choice card, pick an option.
how_it_should_work: Follow-ups appear only if the user setting for follow-up suggestions is on, the last reply is longer than 20 characters, it is not generating or failed, and either follow-ups are enabled for the surface or the last turn searched the web.
They are hidden in temporary chats' generation and any follow-up that asks for a web search is dropped when search was unavailable.
The clarify tool is offered only for short messages with no attachment, URL or code, and is not offered for research runs; choices that are only about format, tone or length are rejected.

features.name: Source cards, citations and source lists
features.use: Show where an answer came from, let the user peek at a source, expand the whole list and open the original page.
how_people_use_it: Click a citation number in the answer: a hover or tap card shows title, site and snippet; click again to open the page in a new tab.
Click the globe button (Open sources panel) to see 'Citations' and 'More' lists as cards.

how_it_works.detail: On the web app the Search dialog waits for 2 or more characters, then calls the search service with the query, category and filters. In chat, Cmd/Ctrl+F opens the in-chat find bar. In the composer, web search is switched on automatically if the model or service has a search route.

how_it_works.step: In-chat find works on the loaded messages
how_it_works.detail: The list finds which message groups contain the text, scrolls to the row and shows a count. Nothing goes to the server.

The service sends GET /api/search with q, limit, category, role, dates, includeArchived, and merges chat, project, file, schedule and indexed-document results into one list, dropping duplicate documents.

how_it_works.step: Server searches the user's own data
how_it_works.detail: The route applies a rate limit, opens a database handle scoped to the user and workspace, checks the data region, validates filters, then runs title, message, project, file and schedule text searches (case-insensitive 'contains') and an indexed document search in parallel. guide.what_it_is_for: A person asks a question and the product runs a multi-step research job. It makes a plan, searches the web (and optionally the person's own files and connected work apps), then writes a cited report. The person can edit the plan, steer or pause the run, read the report, export it, and find it again later. It matters because it turns a long reading job into one reviewed, sourced document.
guide.who_uses_it: Paid Cloud plans only. The server allows Deep Research on pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise (PRO_TIERS in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341,355). Free users get a 403 "plan_upgrade_required" (request-processor.ts:1503-1520). The model must also support research: a research flag, or tools plus a context window of at least 500,000 (apps/web/features/chat/lib/research-capability-gate.ts). Reports belong to one user and are protected by row-level security (migration 0094).

how_it_should_work: The toggle is hidden or turned off if the model cannot do research. It is also off for free-trial users and for plans without the capability, with an upgrade hint.
The server refuses a free plan with 403 plan_upgrade_required.

Limits from the loop defaults: 6 model calls, 12 searches, 4 minutes of searching, 3 tool calls at once. Environment values can change them within fixed ranges.

If the model cannot do research the turn says so and falls back to a normal answer (fallback reason research_unsupported_model).
If the person's tool lockdown is on, research is refused with code lockdown_blocks_research.

how_it_works.detail: The composer shows the toggle only when the model supports research and the plan allows it, and turns it off if the model changes.
The chat page sends research true with the model and, on retry or plan start, the resume data and source choices.

The request schema accepts research, research_sources and research_resume. A free plan is refused, domain rules are merged with workspace rules, and research mode is allowed only if the model supports it.

The route checks budget and workspace policy, blocks secrets, creates an agent run record, loads connector permissions and searches the person's files. If the plan is approved and durable runs are on, it starts a durable workflow; otherwise it streams in the request.

First turn makes the plan and questions; with approval required it stops at awaiting_approval. After approval it runs search rounds within the limits, reads connector and file sources, then writes a cited report. It checks for cancel and pause at each boundary.
Files come from the retrieval index; connected apps are read through their search and fetch tools; all are added to one list so citations share numbers.

The stream sends status, plan and gaps events; the chat shows them in the status bar and step list. Pause and steer go to separate run endpoints.
GET /api/research/reports returns one report or a page of them for the signed-in user. The web gallery and the mobile screen call it.
The report view builds contents from headings, links citations, offers Markdown, PDF and Word export and Run again.

features.name: Create and manage agents
features.use: Make a new agent, edit it, rename it or delete it. Versioning, duplication and ownership transfer are not built.
how_people_use_it: Run /agents create <name> (add --global to save it for every project) to get a blank template file.
Or describe the agent in plain words at the interactive prompt, and the model drafts the name, description and instructions.
Change a field with /agents set <name> <field> <value>; rename with /agents rename <name> <new-name>.
Delete with /agents delete <name> --yes. Without --yes it only warns.
Run /agents validate to list duplicate names, bad colours, unknown permission modes and skills that are not installed.
how_it_should_work: Create writes <slug>.md with starter frontmatter (maxTurns 20, permissionMode default). It refuses if the file already exists, and refuses a name with no letters or numbers.
Delete removes the file for good (no Trash, no archive), after a warning that it cannot be undone.
Should: changes are versioned and restorable, an agent can be duplicated, and an agent can be retired or handed to another owner with its history. None of this exists.
features.on_each_app: CLI done for create, edit, rename, delete. Versioning (S61.21), duplication (S61.23) and retirement or transfer (S61.24) are missing everywhere, CLI included. Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome have no agent management.

features.name: Agent instructions and agent conversation
features.use: Give each agent its own instructions, then work with the session acting as that agent.
how_people_use_it: Write the instructions as the markdown body of the agent file, or use /agents set <name> prompt <text>.
Pick the agent in the /agents picker, or start the CLI with --agent <name>.
Then chat as normal.
how_it_should_work: Activating an agent applies its model, tool allow and deny lists, MCP server list, max turns, permission mode, spend cap and skills to the current session. It does not clear the chat history.
The instructions are added as a system message wrapped in an agent_system_prompt tag.
A file in a repository can only keep or tighten the session's permission mode, never loosen it. If it asks for a looser mode, the session keeps its own and a message is printed.
The chat shows 'Agent `name` activated' and, if the agent sets a model, the model now in use.
Should: a separate conversation per agent. The code switches the one session into that agent. I saw no separate per-agent thread.
features.on_each_app: CLI done. The CLI also has --agent-id to resume or bind to an agent thread id. Other apps: missing.

features.name: Shared tools, skills and per-agent limits
features.use: Agents use the tools and skills the account already has, but each agent can be narrowed and capped.
how_people_use_it: Set tools, disallowedTools, skills, mcp servers, maxTurns and maxBudgetUsd in the agent file, or with /agents set.
maxBudgetUsd takes a positive dollar amount such as 0.50.
/agents validate warns about skills that are not installed.
how_it_should_work: Tool allow list: if the user started the CLI with its own allow list, the agent's list is intersected with it, so it can only narrow.

Skills named in the agent are looked up among the installed skills, case-insensitively, and each match is added as a system message. Names not installed are skipped silently when running and reported only by /agents validate.
Spend cap: the lower of the session cap and the agent cap wins. Max turns are set from the agent file.
Team spend is pooled. Teammates share the remaining headroom, and a teammate stops and tells the lead when the cap is used up.
features.on_each_app: CLI done. All other apps: missing. The brief marks the spend and turn limits as done only for the CLI, with no screen to set them outside the command line.

features.name: Agent memory, workspace, routines and responsibilities
features.use: Planned: each agent would have its own memory, scheduled routines, private workspace and a list of what it owns.
how_people_use_it: Not possible today.
how_it_should_work: Should: separate memory per agent, routines that run as the agent, a private workspace and a responsibility list. Nothing in the agent code does any of this.
features.on_each_app: Missing on all six apps.

features.name: Agent teams, delegation and coordinator
features.use: Run several agents on one job. A lead agent hands work to teammates or one-off specialist subagents and gets the results back. Agents can message each other.
how_people_use_it: Start the CLI with --team or set AGI_TEAM=1.
The lead model calls spawn_teammate with a name, a prompt and optionally an installed agent name to use as the teammate's definition.
The model uses send_message, read_messages, team_task and list_teammates. The user watches the thread in the chat.
For a one-off specialist the model calls the agent tool with action list, then run.
how_it_should_work: Team off: spawn_teammate refuses with 'Agent teams are off. Start agi with --team or AGI_TEAM=1.' Only the lead can spawn teammates.
The names lead and user are reserved. Names must pass a strict safe-character check.

A message to an unknown or stopped teammate fails with a clear error. Messages from other agents are labelled 'another agent on your team, not the person', and the teammate is told they never count as the person's approval.
Each teammate runs in its own thread with its own session. It reports to the lead when it finishes, or if it could not start.
The shared task list has the states pending, in progress, completed, blocked, with dependencies.

A named specialist can only narrow the parent's authority. Its model and permission-mode overrides are ignored, tool lists are intersected with the parent's, deny lists are joined, and max turns can only go down.
Limit: the lead's tool catalog for the agent tool lists at most 200 agents and about 18 KB, and hides prompt bodies, paths, model and permission mode.
features.on_each_app: CLI done. Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome: missing.

features.name: Presence indicator and pause or disable
features.use: Planned: see whether each agent is working, idle or offline, and pause an agent so it stops acting.
how_people_use_it: Not possible for saved agents today.
how_it_should_work: Should: a status next to each name in the roster, and a way to switch an agent off until it is switched back on.

What exists is only for live teammates in a team session: status Active, Idle or Completed, and a stop flag. When a teammate goes idle, a TeammateIdle hook fires. That status is not shown on the roster and cannot be set by the user. It disappears when the session ends.
features.on_each_app: Missing on all apps per the brief. The team status inside the CLI is partial and is not a roster indicator.

features.name: Escalation to the user
features.use: When an agent needs a decision or approval, it stops and asks the person, and the person gets told even when away from the screen.
how_people_use_it: CLI: an approval prompt appears in the chat. A teammate's prompt starts with its name, for example 'alice: ...'.
Mobile: a push alert says 'Approval needed' or 'Your agent has a question'. Tapping it opens the Tasks screen with that run.
The same alert appears in the in-app notification feed and, for a signed-in browser, as a web push.
how_it_should_work: The agent waits for the answer.
Server side, an event of approval_required, input_required, completed or failed writes a feed notification and sends a push. Run finished and failed alerts are de-duplicated per run.
Mobile alerts can be turned off by an explicit false in the mobilePushAgentActivity preference. The default is on.
Failure: if sending fails, it logs a warning and returns pushed false. It never throws into the run.
The Mobile Tasks route only opens a run when the app is in Cloud mode and Cloud is unlocked for the user.
features.on_each_app: CLI done. Mobile done (alerts and the Tasks screen). Web: the brief says missing, but the server code that sends the alert is on web. VS Code, Chrome, Desktop: missing.

features.name: Agent activity history
features.use: Review what each agent did: when, how it ended, how many files it changed and what it cost.
how_people_use_it: Run /agents history for all agents, or /agents history <name> for one. Aliases: activity, log.
how_it_should_work: Shows the 20 newest runs first with local date and time, agent name, outcome (completed, failed or cancelled), files changed and spend, plus the error text when there is one.
Empty state: 'No recorded runs for agent `name` yet.' or 'No recorded agent runs yet.'
Only runs of a named agent are listed. A subagent with no agent name is skipped.
The record keeps only the prompt length, not the prompt text.
features.on_each_app: CLI done. All other apps: missing.

how_it_works.detail: An agent is a markdown file with frontmatter. Fields are name, description, model, tools, disallowed tools, max turns, permission mode, colour, skills, spend cap and MCP servers. The body is the system prompt.

discover_agents reads the user folders (the CLI config folder's agents directory and ~/.claude/agents), then the current project's agents if the project is trusted, then plugin agents. Project and user agents are merged.
/agents with no argument opens the picker. Subcommands (list, show, path, create, validate, history, delete, rename, set) are handled by render_agents_command.
Create writes a template file. Set, rename and delete rewrite or remove the file after checks. The model can also draft an agent from a description.
Picking a row reloads the definition from that exact file, then applies it to the live session: model, tools, MCP servers, turns, permission mode (never looser), spend cap, system prompt and skills.

The model's agent tool lists agents (a trimmed catalog) or runs one. A run is handled by the subagent manager, which applies the named agent with the narrower-only rules and runs it on its own thread.
Team mode is read from --team or AGI_TEAM. spawn_teammate checks the lead, the names and the spend cap, then TeamManager.launch registers the teammate, starts its thread, and shares the spend pool.

send_message checks that both sides are on the team and that the target has not stopped, then puts the message in the mailbox and the shared transcript. A teammate's tool approvals go to the user's approval sink with the teammate's name added.
Each finished subagent run is appended to subagents.jsonl in the config folder. /agents history reads it back newest first.
For cloud agent runs, the web server records a feed notification and sends a push (Expo and web). The phone opens the Tasks route, which opens the run.

key_files.role: Agent file format, discovery, applying an agent to a session, and every /agents subcommand.
Team manager: teammates, mailboxes, shared tasks, spend pool, teammate threads and the team tools.
Runs one-off subagents (including named agents) on their own thread and records the audit entry.
Writes and reads the subagent run log used by /agents history.
The /agents picker overlay: filter, list, empty states, colour.
Handles picker keys and activates the chosen agent in the session.
The chat loop: spawn_teammate tool and classification of task and named-agent calls.
Runs the agent tool (list action) and routes run to the orchestrator.
Command line flags --agent, --agent-id, --team and the AGI_TEAM check.
Turns agent run events into feed notifications and push alerts.
Mobile route that opens the cloud run an alert points to.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area decides which AI model answers each message. In Auto, the app picks a model from the request, the person's plan, cost and the health of each provider route. A person can also pin one model, set a default model for a project, compare answers side by side, and see which model answered and why. It matters because cost, privacy and plan limits are enforced here, and a chosen model must not be swapped without the person knowing.
guide.who_uses_it: Every user of the six apps uses Auto and the model picker. In Cloud (our managed service) the plan tier decides which models are allowed (tierAdmissionRejection in packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts), and the Free plan has its own cheap lane (apps/web/lib/services/free-lane/mode.ts). Workspace admins set model and privacy rules that routing obeys (apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx). Developers using the CLI get extra flags (--auto, --provider, --fallback-model, --agent). The public API uses the same server router as web chat.

features.name: Auto picks the model
features.use: Auto chooses one model and one provider route per message, so the person does not have to. It only chooses among models the person is allowed to use and can afford.
how_people_use_it: Open the model picker and choose Auto (the default).
Type and send. Nothing else to do.
In the CLI, run agi --auto (Cloud sessions only).
how_it_should_work: Candidates are filtered first: model must be live, not retired, allowed for the plan tier, allowed by workspace policy, allowed in the region, and have a usable credential (evaluateEligibility in auto.ts, around line 1340).
Then candidates are ranked. When one model has several provider routes, one route is chosen by health, cost and cache reuse (slotRouteCost and rankRoutes in auto.ts).

If the person has a credit budget, models whose estimated cost is above the remaining credits are dropped (isAffordable, auto.ts:1682). If the balance cannot be read, routing goes on without this check (request-processor.ts:4607-4612).
A task family such as code or research gives a named profile (Instant, High, Code, Research) that weighs quality, cost and speed (packages/ai/routing/src/profiles/index.ts).
If no route works, the result is an 'unavailable' decision with reasons, not a silent guess.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop (shows the hosted web app) and the public API use the server router in the chat completions route. Mobile and Chrome run the same shared router on the device before sending (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/cloudDispatchRouting.ts, apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedChatRouting.ts). The CLI uses a Rust version through the model registry crate (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:667-740). VS Code has Auto rows in its picker (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:441-460). Brief status: done on all.

features.name: Instant, Best and Economy choices
features.use: Next to Auto, a person can bias routing toward speed (Instant), capability (Best) or low cost (Economy).
how_people_use_it: Web: open the model picker, pick Auto, then choose Instant, Best or Economy (ComposerFooter.tsx around lines 1639-1680).
VS Code: pick a row named 'Auto · Instant', 'Auto · Best' or 'Auto · Economy'.
CLI: the profile ids are auto, speed, quality, cost (apps/cli/src/routing/profile.rs:3).
how_it_should_work: Instant sends routing_profile 'speed'; the server then prefers the fastest slots (speedFirstSlots in speed-first-slots.ts) and the economy band.
Best maps to the premium band; Economy maps to the economy band (PROFILE_BAND in routing-profile-choice.ts).
The choice never lets a model past plan or policy limits.
'Auto' sends no profile at all (useChatStream.ts:4646-4649).
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code and the API have it. Mobile's request type carries routing_profile (apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts:567) but I did not find a picker for it; the brief does not list mobile for these. Chrome: the brief lists cost-first only.

features.name: Understanding the request
features.use: Each message is labelled by kind (coding, research, agentic, image-bearing, long and so on) so routing can match a model to the work.
how_people_use_it: Nothing to do. Type normally, attach images, or switch on Research, Code or Work toggles.
how_it_should_work: A word-pattern classifier looks at the text, attachments and token count (classifyTaskLocally in classify.ts). It forces long-context past a token budget and sends images to multimodal models.
Explicit toggles override the text: research on gives research; Work mode or office creation gives agentic; code execution gives coding (resolveToolAwareTaskType, request-processor.ts:1032-1043).
A second step groups the request into a 'task family' from structural signals; if the signals are unclear it returns no family and the normal Auto policy runs unchanged (task-family.ts:160-200).
Words like 'latest' or 'today' count as research signals (RE_RESEARCH in classify.ts).
There is no model-based classifier: confidence is advisory and routing uses the type only (classify.ts header). If nothing matches, a default general type is used.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop and API classify on the server. Mobile, Chrome and VS Code import the same TypeScript classifier (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/routingTask.ts:1,19). The CLI has a hand-kept Rust copy (apps/cli/src/routing/classify.rs) that tests keep in step. All marked done.

features.name: Pick a model yourself, and locks
features.use: A person can pin a named model so the request runs on it. The CLI can also pin the provider.
how_people_use_it: Open the model picker and choose a model; it applies to the conversation.
CLI: agi --model <id>, or --provider <name> to force the provider.
Mobile, VS Code and Chrome: use the model picker.
how_it_should_work: A named model goes through the same eligibility checks. If it fails, the result is 'explicit_model_ineligible' or 'model_not_available_in_region' with reasons (auto.ts:1840-1850), not a swap.
A route can be pinned only with an explicit model, never with an Auto alias (auto.ts:1745-1756).
On the web, the out-of-credits path does not swap the model when a route was pinned (request-processor.ts:6052).
Provider lock and route lock are not offered on Mobile, VS Code or Chrome. A route pin exists in the server request (requiredRouteId) but I found no screen for it.
features.on_each_app: Pick-a-model: done everywhere. Provider lock: CLI only (--provider, apps/cli/src/lib.rs:194). Route lock: no app screen found (brief: mobile, vscode, chrome missing). See things_that_look_wrong for cases where an explicit model is still swapped.

features.name: Project default model
features.use: A project can store a default model, and new chats in that project start on it.
how_people_use_it: Web: open project settings and use the 'Default model' field (ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx).
Start a new chat inside the project; the model is applied for you.
VS Code: apply a project; the chat model can switch to the project's default (projectActions.ts:405-406).
how_it_should_work: The field only lists models the plan allows and drops 'coming soon' ones (ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx:21-37).
On a new chat the default is applied once per project (WebChatPage.tsx:2125-2140).
If the saved default is no longer listed, the field still shows the current value (currentListed check).
features.on_each_app: Web and Desktop: done. Mobile: reads defaultModelId from the project store (apps/mobile/stores/projects/cloudProjectStore.ts:26,152; chat.tsx:315). VS Code: done. CLI and Chrome: none.

features.name: Privacy-first routing
features.use: Keep requests on the device, or only on providers that do not keep or train on them.
how_people_use_it: Choose a Local on-device model in the picker.
Admins set privacy modes in workspace policy (WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:73,239-245).
CLI: Local sessions refuse to send anything off the device.
how_it_should_work: There is no single 'privacy-first' button. It is built from trust mode (local, on-device, own key, Cloud), the zero-data-retention rule and the no-training opt-out.
With zero-data-retention on, only routes that support it are kept (auto.ts:1099-1107). With no-training only, providers that may train on inputs are dropped (evaluateEligibility).
If no provider is left after the no-training filter, the request fails with a clear message (request-processor.ts:4697-4700).
A Local CLI session blocks a model that would go to Cloud or own key and tells the person to use /continue-with-cloud or /continue-with-byok (validate_privacy_boundary in apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs).
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code: done. Chrome and API: not listed in the brief.

features.name: Health, fallback and switch offers
features.use: When a route is failing, Auto avoids it. When a call fails, the app falls back or offers a one-click way to another model.
how_people_use_it: Nothing for automatic fallback.
Web: click 'Use <image model>' or 'Switch to a cloud model' in the notices above the composer.
VS Code: a 'switch model' action appears on some errors.
CLI: errors say to run again with --fallback-model, or give a model chain with commas (a,b,c).
how_it_should_work: Observed health of each route lowers its rank (observedRoutePenalty, auto.ts:937). Turn it off with AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH=0.
Same-model fallbacks come first, then another model (MAX_SAME_MODEL_FALLBACKS_BEFORE_SUBSTITUTION in auto.ts).
CLI: the chain only rotates on rate-limit, network or server errors, not on bad auth or bad requests (apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs:12-26).
A switch offer must be explicit: the person clicks; nothing flips by itself.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile (alert with 'Use <model>', alertBlockedImageRequest.ts:16), CLI, VS Code (errorPresentation.ts:479-493): done per the brief. Chrome: fallback listed, switch offer not listed.

features.name: Which model answered, and why
features.use: Each answer shows the model that wrote it. If Auto moved to another model, a short line says why. Each decision also carries the policy version that made it.
how_people_use_it: Read the model name on the answer.
If shown, read the line 'Moved to <model>: <reason>'.
how_it_should_work: The line is built from the moved-from model, the reason code and the served model (modelEscalation.ts:32-80). Reason codes map to plain phrases (auto-route-explanation.ts:1-12).
It is a receipt, shown once after the answer finishes (MessageBubble.tsx:3511).
Each decision builds a trace with policyVersion (routing-trace.ts:16,154). The web server saves it to a table so a turn can be traced later.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile (messageTurnNotices.ts:47, MessageBubble.tsx:816), CLI (prints 'Auto route: ... -> ...', chat.rs:732-735), Chrome (bubbles.ts:474) and API: done. VS Code: missing for explanation and attribution. Policy versioning: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, API.

features.name: Compare models side by side
features.use: Send one prompt to several models and read the answers next to each other.
how_people_use_it: Web: open /models/compare, or choose models in the model catalogue and use Compare.
Type one prompt and send.
Mobile: open Compare and send the prompt to two models.
how_it_should_work: Web needs 2 to 3 models (compare-answers.ts:5-6). Each answer shows queued, streaming, done, stopped or failed (use-compare-answers.ts:8).
A failed model shows 'This model could not answer. Try again.' without stopping the others.

features.name: Specialist workers with their own model
features.use: The CLI can run a custom agent that uses its own model, tools and budget.
how_people_use_it: Create a markdown file in .agiworkforce/agents/ or ~/.agiworkforce/agents/ with front matter (name, model, tools, max turns, budget).
Run agi --agent <name>, or use /agents in the REPL.
how_it_should_work: The file sets the session model, allowed tools and spend cap (AgentDefinition and cap_spend in apps/cli/src/agents.rs).

features.on_each_app: CLI only. Mobile and Chrome: missing. Web, Desktop, VS Code: not listed in the brief.

features.name: Not built
features.use: Advisor escalation, abstaining when unsure, a pluggable classifier adapter and a routing evaluation dashboard are marked not applicable in every app.
how_people_use_it: Nothing to use.
how_it_should_work: Do not expect these. The classifier has no model fallback by design (classify.ts header). Decision traces are stored (see data_kept), but I found no dashboard that reads them.
features.on_each_app: Not applicable in any app per the brief.

how_it_works.step: Person chooses a model or Auto
how_it_works.detail: The picker stores the choice. On web it also stores the routing choice (auto, speed, quality, cost). Project defaults are applied on a new chat.
The web hook adds routing_profile only when it is not 'auto'. Mobile and Chrome first run the shared router on the device. The CLI resolves Auto itself for the launch prompt.
The server classifies the text and attachments, lets explicit toggles override it, then adds a task family.

In parallel it reads route health, conversation route history, zero-data-retention policy, workspace model policy, the user's saved routing preference and residency region. It also reads credit balance for the affordability check.

resolveAutoRoute checks trust mode, capabilities and runtime profile. A named model is checked and used as is; an Auto alias goes to eligibility filtering, then ordering by profile and task family, then route ranking. Fallbacks are attached.

how_it_works.step: Server records the decision and sends the call
how_it_works.detail: A trace with the policy version is built and saved without blocking the turn. Failover routes are built from the decision. Out of credits, a cheaper model may replace the one asked for unless a route was pinned.
The stream carries the served model and, if it moved, the moved-from model and reason. Each app shows the model and an optional 'Moved to' line.
--auto resolves a model for the first prompt and then, for own-key sessions, re-resolves every turn with continuity and prints the change. Cloud sessions are re-resolved by the server.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the router and classifier in packages/ai/routing (used by web server, mobile, Chrome and VS Code), the model registry in packages/ai/model-registry, the profile choices in packages/contracts/types/src/routing-profile-choice.ts, the 'Moved to' line in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/modelEscalation.ts and the reason phrases in packages/contracts/types/src/auto-route-explanation.ts. Separate: the CLI has Rust copies of the router, classifier and profiles (crates/agiworkforce-model-registry, apps/cli/src/routing/*), kept in line by tests. The web server adds credit, workspace policy, residency, free lane and trace saving (request-processor.ts). Each app has its own picker screen. The public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it follows the web path.

things_that_look_wrong.what: The brief says an explicit model is never silently swapped (S79.16), but Mobile and Chrome call the router with fallbackToAutoForCapabilityMismatch true. A pinned model that lacks a needed capability is moved to Auto with reason 'capability_fallback'. The web server turns this off for exact selections.

On the web, a person who named a model and has no credits left can get a cheaper model instead (reason 'insufficient_credits'), unless a route was pinned. It is reported in message metadata, but it is still a swap of a chosen model.

Many code references in the brief point to the wrong place. ComposerFooter.tsx:278 is a thinking-effort helper, not Auto routing. ModelRow.tsx:166 is an accessibility hint. apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:234 is a quota warning parser, not a provider lock. request-processor.ts line numbers have moved (the file is over 7000 lines).
The user routing preference (us_only) is read on every chat turn, but its own comment says nothing yet offers a control to set it and the route has no caller.
The migration that creates the decision trace table says 'NOT YET APPLIED: draft only', which may be stale or true; the code writes to the table either way.
Mobile's request type accepts routing_profile, but the brief lists no mobile status for speed and quality, and I found no mobile control that sets it.
The CLI fallback-trigger enum is marked allow(dead_code), which hints some variants are unused.
The classifier's header says its accuracy is far lower than its old 75 to 85 percent claim, and it has no model fallback. Routing quality for ambiguous text depends on a weak heuristic.
In the CLI, per-turn re-resolution only changes the model for own-key sessions. Cloud, Local and on-device sessions return without switching (Cloud is left to the server).
